explanations.explanation: Close, but Jesus doesn't say that. He says, "So practice and observe everything they tell you." (Matthew 23:3) The seat of Moses, Israel's leader, is why their teaching still counts. Ignoring all of it would be tossing the whole batch because one cook was sloppy.

Right, baker. Jesus says, "So practice and observe everything they tell you." (Matthew 23:3) The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat, and that's why their teaching still counts. What He warns about is copying how they live, and that comes next.

explanations.answer: They do not practice what they preach
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Jesus says, "But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach." (Matthew 23:3) The words are fine to follow. The living is the part that doesn't match. That's like me handing out a cookie recipe while I eat store-bought. Which, hey, I won't.

explanations.answer: They copy the customs of foreigners
explanations.explanation: Nothing like that in the passage, baker. Jesus gives His reason right in the verse: "for they do not practice what they preach." (Matthew 23:3) The problem is that their actions don't match their words. Foreigners never come up.

explanations.answer: They do not keep the Sabbath day
explanations.explanation: That's a fair guess, but it's not what Jesus says here. His reason is, "for they do not practice what they preach." (Matthew 23:3) Nothing in these verses mentions the Sabbath. The gap is between what they say and what they do.

explanations.answer: They will not lift a finger
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Jesus says they "are not willing to lift a finger to move them." (Matthew 23:4) They pile on the load and then watch. I think that's the worst kind of helper: all opinions, no oven mitts.

explanations.answer: They carry half of the load
explanations.explanation: Nice and generous, but that's not what Jesus says. He says they "are not willing to lift a finger to move them." (Matthew 23:4) Half would be a whole lot more than a finger. They carry none.

explanations.answer: They help only on feast days
explanations.explanation: Good try, but the text doesn't mention feast days. Jesus says they "are not willing to lift a finger to move them." (Matthew 23:4) No holiday exceptions, no part-time help.

You got it, baker. Jesus says, "All their deeds are done for men to see." (Matthew 23:5) The good deeds are really a show. I've stamped cookies for an audience before, but my mustache didn't need the applause.

explanations.answer: So the poor will be fed
explanations.explanation: I wish that were the answer, friend. But Jesus says, "All their deeds are done for men to see." (Matthew 23:5) Feeding the poor never comes up here. Their aim is being seen.
Not quite, baker. Jesus gives a different purpose: "All their deeds are done for men to see." (Matthew 23:5) The audience He names is people, not God. Forgiveness isn't mentioned in these verses.
Yes, baker. Jesus says, "They love the places of honor at banquets." (Matthew 23:6) Those are the best spots at the table. I think they'd check the seating chart before they checked the guest list.
Ha, that one would've changed the whole sermon, friend. But Jesus says they love "the places of honor at banquets." (Matthew 23:6) Honor is the word. Service is what He lifts up later, in verse 11.
It sounds nice, baker, but it's not the word. Jesus says they love "the places of honor at banquets." (Matthew 23:6) It's about the best seats, not about welcoming anybody.

True, baker! Jesus says they love "the chief seats in the synagogues." (Matthew 23:6) The synagogue is where people gathered to worship and hear the Scriptures. Even there, they're after the front row.
Not this time, friend. Jesus says they love "the chief seats in the synagogues." (Matthew 23:6) The synagogue is where people gathered to worship and hear the Scriptures. So the statement is true.

explanations.answer: They have one Teacher and are all brothers
explanations.explanation: Right, baker. Jesus says, "for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers." (Matthew 23:8) Nobody in the group sits above the others. The one Teacher is Jesus, as verse 10 shows.

explanations.answer: The title belongs only to the priests
explanations.explanation: Good guess, but the priests don't appear here. Jesus says, "for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers." (Matthew 23:8) His reason is about who the Teacher is, and about being brothers.

explanations.answer: They have not studied long enough yet
explanations.explanation: That's not the reason Jesus gives, friend. He says, "for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers." (Matthew 23:8) Nothing here is about how much anyone has studied. It's about having one Teacher.

Yes, baker. Jesus says, "And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven." (Matthew 23:9) The one Father is in heaven. I'd never argue with that, since my own kids called me Papa.

Close in sound, but no, friend. Jesus actually says in verse 8 that "you are all brothers." In verse 9 He says, "do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven." (Matthew 23:9)

Neighbor is a nice word, baker, but it isn't in this verse. Jesus says, "do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven." (Matthew 23:9) The one in heaven is the Father.
That's right, baker. Jesus says, "for you have one Instructor, the Christ." (Matthew 23:10) Christ means the Anointed One, the Messiah. Every other teacher is a student next to Him.

Moses, Israel's leader, comes up in verse 2, so I see the pull. But Jesus says, "for you have one Instructor, the Christ." (Matthew 23:10) Moses' seat is where the scribes and Pharisees sit. The one Instructor is the Christ.
Elijah is a great name, baker, but he's not in this passage. Jesus says, "for you have one Instructor, the Christ." (Matthew 23:10) The Christ is the one Instructor.

explanations.answer: The one who is your servant
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker! Jesus says, "The greatest among you shall be your servant." (Matthew 23:11) The great one is the one who serves. That flips the banquet seating chart right over.

explanations.answer: The one with the best seat
explanations.explanation: That's the Pharisees' answer, friend, not Jesus'. They love "the chief seats in the synagogues." (Matthew 23:6) Jesus says, "The greatest among you shall be your servant." (Matthew 23:11)

explanations.answer: The one who teaches the most
explanations.explanation: I get why you'd pick it, baker. But Jesus says, "The greatest among you shall be your servant." (Matthew 23:11) Greatness is about serving, not about how much someone teaches.

Not quite, friend. Jesus says the opposite: "For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted." (Matthew 23:12) Lifting yourself up leads to being humbled. It's the one who humbles himself who gets exalted.

Right, baker. Jesus says, "For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted." (Matthew 23:12) Whoever exalts himself will be humbled. Whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
